findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored without enforced encryption at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing public access block / no access control
findings.description: No ACL or bucket policy restricting access is defined, and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource to prevent the bucket from becoming publicly accessible.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for a bucket storing ledger exports, leaving potentially sensitive financial data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so model artifacts are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for a bucket holding operational runbooks, which could contain sensitive operational details, leaving it unencrypted at rest.

The bucket uses the canned ACL 'log-delivery-write', which grants write and read-ACP permissions to the S3 log delivery group; combined with force_destroy this increases risk of unauthorized write access to the audit trail bucket if not tightly scoped.

This object is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.reports_archive, which has no server-side encryption configured, so the vendor roster file (potentially containing sensitive vendor data) is stored unencrypted.
force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be deleted without recovery, removing a safeguard against accidental or malicious data loss on a bucket with no versioning enabled.
